newsitem.title: USA: General Instrument set for summer spin-off.
newsitem.headline: General Instrument set for summer spin-off.

text.p: General Instrument Corp, which Monday reported a loss in the fourth quarter ended December 31, said it expects to complete its restructuring into three independent companies to be completed this summer.
The company said it lost $17.1 million, or $0.12 a share, compared to net income of $53.4 million, or $0.43, a year ago.

General Instrument said the latest results included previously announced after-tax charges of $59 million tied to investments in its next generation of digital products, a write-down of assets and costs of the restructuring plan.

The company said two of the three companies being spun off, NextLevel Systems Inc and CommScope Inc, are expected to continue their positive sales momentum in 1997. The General Semiconductor Inc operation is also showing signs of resuming its long-term global growth, General Instrument said.
General Instrument makes set-top cable boxes and other telecommunications products.
Its shares closed up 1/4 Monday at 24-5/8.
